trickyParts: Four tests of internal/dispatch/redeliver (the redeliverTestLeases ones) migrate into the database their DSN names rather than making one per test, so they fail `permission denied for schema public` against $LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN, whose database this pod's login does not own. Run the package with DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5433/legion_test_infra627?sslmode=disable, a database made for this issue and left in place. That is the pod, not the branch.
-race needs cgo on this pod: prefix CGO_ENABLED=1, since go env CGO_ENABLED is 0 here.

The freshness rule's loop in Importer.Sync terminates in at most two rounds only because golang.org/x/sync/singleflight deletes the key before it sends a result, so a flight joined on the second round necessarily began after the caller asked. The comment at the loop records that dependence on a third-party internal; Group.Forget is never called for the key.

The index's safety rests on two things that must stay together: an entry is never keyed before the moment it is written (pendingFor floors it at the sweep's now), and cursorOverlap (2 min) covers the under-a-minute a selected but unacted entry can fall behind the cursor. A change to either breaks the floor argument in openDue's comment.
openDue must not repair under a dry run: Options.DryRun writes nothing, and a stray entry deleted as it is read would be a write. TestAContinuousDryRunLeavesAStrayIndexEntry holds that.

The evidence harness is /legion/scratch/tmp/infra627 (build.sh, e1.sh, e2.sh, e2-bytes.sh, e2-dryrun.sh, fakegh/, kvseed/, out/, logs/). It builds each envoy-dispatch from a git archive export of its commit, so re-running it at another head is one edit of build.sh's HEAD_COMMIT. The load reproduction's own stack is /legion/scratch/tmp/dispatch-loadtest, seeded (template dispatch_seed, migration 161) and left running; its E-3 output is under /legion/scratch/tmp/e3.
deviations: The spec's 2i names the index key as pending.<GUID> with the due time in the value. The due time is in the key instead (pending.<YYYYMMDD>.<HH>.<MM>.<GUID>), because a JetStream KV selects only by subject filter, so a watch of pending.* would still stream one message per open entry and the cost would still grow with entries that are open and not due. Recorded as departure 1 of the plan; the outcome is unchanged.

The spec's 2h asks for a test that a slow fake GitHub does not block a read of the model. That is already true before the change: getArchitectureTree reads the pool directly and the importer holds no pooled connection across a GitHub call. It is answered by a labelled guard (database.Pool.Use().InUse == 0 while a sync waits on GitHub) whose comment says so, folded into TestASlowSourceDoesNotBlockAnotherSourceOfItsProject. Recorded as departure 2 of the plan.

The before/after line on the committed load reproduction can only show no regression, because neither changed path runs under that harness (it builds Dispatch with no GitHub App key, so the sweeper never starts and the importer idles, and the route mix names no architecture route) and neither change touches Postgres. It was run as written, three runs a side with every run and the median; the numbers that show the win are E-1, E-2 and the benchmark. Recorded as departure 3 of the plan.

One behaviour change of the importer the spec does not name: a caller that goes away no longer suppresses the record of its sync's deadline on the source row. A shared flight has no single caller, and the row is read by the five-minute ticker and the Settings page. Recorded as departure 4 of the plan; the second half of TestSyncDeadlineIsRecordedOnTheRow is the test.

Lookback grows from 60 to 66 minutes (maxBackoff + 3*Interval). The plan does not name it; the index requires it, because a record is now read when it is due rather than on every sweep, so the listing window must outlast the longest backoff or the sweep that reads a record no longer sees GitHub's answer to its last request. INFRA-514's architect accepted it at 2026-11-01T19:55:54Z and asked for it in the pull request's change list.

The benchmark's ratio criterion is not met: index is 2.40x ns/op, 8.81x B/op and 16.05x allocs/op for ten times the entries, against the plan's 1.3x and 1.2x. The residual is nats-server's per-subject work for the filtered consumer, measured in-process, not work per entry. INFRA-514's architect decided at 2026-11-01T19:55:54Z that this is a recorded departure with no bucket of its own and no child issue, and asked for the measurement to stand in the pull request body as taken.
openQuestions: None blocking. The architect has both findings above and has answered both.
discoveredComplexity: The index would have introduced a defect the plan did not foresee: a delivery GitHub recovered while its record waited out the longest backoff was asked for again every hour until it expired undelivered with a false ERROR, because the listing window equalled the longest backoff. Found by reading why a worker had to widen an existing test's clock advance, reproduced with a two-minute sweep loop whose ticks do not land on the due minute (an eighth redelivery request for a delivery whose seventh was answered 200), and fixed with Lookback = maxBackoff + 3*Interval. TestADeliveryRecoveredDuringTheLongestBackoffIsDeliveredAndAskedForNoMore fails against the old constant.

openUnlisted did not honour nats.go's three ways of ending a watch: a scan its idle timer ended read as a complete one, so a short scan silently under-reported the open deliveries. That is a defect on main in a file this change touches; it is fixed here, and kvwatch.ScanExistingKeys was split so the check lives in one place for all three readers.

`.dispatch/architecture/dispatch-redeliver.md` claimed the bucket holds the last rate limit. It does not: the sweep's backoff is a row of Postgres's github_rate_limits. Corrected with the rest of that sentence.

Dispatch's own numbered migrations collided with main while this branch ran (main was red on TestMigrationSetTakesNumbersThenTimestamps until sjawhar/legion#2633 merged as 0642a37a). The branch carries a forward merge of that fix, whose fingerprint and file set are unchanged either side of the merge; the comment on the pull request records both.
